name: Syllogism
shortcutSummary: Draw Venn diagrams for each statement. For "All A are B" draw A circle completely inside B. For "Some A are B" draw overlapping circles. For "No A is B" draw separate circles. Then check if conclusions follow from all possible valid diagrams.
conceptExplanation:
Syllogism questions give you two or more statements and ask you to determine which conclusions logically follow. This is one of the most important topics for Banking exams (IBPS, SBI) and also appears in SSC.

The Venn diagram method is the most reliable approach — draw circles to represent the relationships described in the statements, then check each conclusion.

subtopics.name: Syllogism — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation:
Syllogism questions give you two or more statements and ask you to determine which conclusions logically follow. This is one of the most important topics for Banking exams (IBPS, SBI) and also appears in SSC.

The Venn diagram method is the most reliable approach — draw circles to represent the relationships described in the statements, then check each conclusion.
shortcuts: Venn Diagram Method: Draw circles for each category. Check all valid configurations.
Negation of All = Some Not: If "All A are B" is false, then "Some A are not B" is true.
Possibility Cases: "Some A may be B" is true unless "No A is B" is explicitly stated. Possibilities are always true unless directly contradicted.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Statements:
1. All Pens are Books.
2. All Books are Papers.

Conclusions:
I. Some Papers are Pens.
II. All Pens are Papers.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
practiceQuestions.hint: Draw Venn diagrams. A conclusion must hold in ALL valid diagrams to be considered true.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Since all Pens are Books and all Books are Papers, the set of Pens is entirely contained within Papers. Hence, All Pens are Papers is true, and Some Papers are Pens is definitely true.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Venn diagram: circle of Pens is inside Books, and circle of Books is inside Papers.
Step 2: Conclusion I ("Some Papers are Pens") holds valid because Pens occupies part of Papers.
Step 3: Conclusion II ("All Pens are Papers") holds valid unconditionally.
Step 4: Both conclusions I and II follow.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Statements:
1. Some Cats are Dogs.
2. All Dogs are Animals.

Conclusions:
I. Some Cats are Animals.
II. All Animals are Cats.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
practiceQuestions.hint: Draw Venn diagrams. A conclusion must hold in ALL valid diagrams to be considered true.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The intersection between Cats and Dogs is entirely inside Animals, ensuring Some Cats are Animals. However, All Animals are Cats cannot be definitively deduced.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Some Cats are Dogs creates an overlap between Cats and Dogs.
Step 2: Since all Dogs are within Animals, the overlapping portion of Cats is also inside Animals. Thus Conclusion I follows.
Step 3: There is no guarantee that all Animals belong to Cats. Conclusion II does not follow.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Statements:
1. All Cars are Vehicles.
2. Some Vehicles are Trucks.

Conclusions:
I. Some Cars are Trucks.
II. Some Trucks are Vehicles.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
practiceQuestions.hint: Draw Venn diagrams. A conclusion must hold in ALL valid diagrams to be considered true.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Some Vehicles are Trucks directly implies Some Trucks are Vehicles (conversion rule). But the overlap of Vehicles and Trucks might not touch Cars, so Some Cars are Trucks cannot be definitively concluded.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Some Vehicles are Trucks allows immediate valid conversion to Some Trucks are Vehicles (Conclusion II follows).
Step 2: There is no direct link between Cars and Trucks. Conclusion I is only possible, not definite.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Statements:
1. No Apples is Fruits.
2. All Fruits are Vegetables.

Conclusions:
I. Some Vegetables are not Apples.
II. No Apples is Vegetables.
options: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
practiceQuestions.hint: Draw Venn diagrams. A conclusion must hold in ALL valid diagrams to be considered true.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The portion of Vegetables that contains Fruits cannot be Apples (because No Apples is Fruits). Therefore, Some Vegetables are not Apples definitely follows. But No Apples is Vegetables does not follow because Apples can overlap with parts of Vegetables outside Fruits.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Set Fruits is disjoint from Apples.
Step 2: All Fruits are in Vegetables, which means at least that part of Vegetables cannot overlap with Apples. Hence Some Vegetables are not Apples follows.
Step 3: Apples may or may not overlap with remaining parts of Vegetables, so definite negative "No Apples is Vegetables" fails.
